classification.difficultyReason: Follow the explicit protractor/compass construction, justify rhombus equality from adjacent equal sides and parallel pairs, then check diagonal bisection/perpendicularity; the construction and measurement tasks are scaffolded.

content.prompt: Construct a rhombus $ABCD$ as follows. Start with the interval $DC$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 construction figure above parts a–b
spec.description: Starting interval DC extends rightwards beyond C. Red dashed construction rays form DA extended above A, CB and AB. Two visible portions of the compass arc centred at D pass through A and C. Three corresponding exterior/interior angle sectors are labelled 70 degrees.
spec.mathematics: DA and CB make 70 degrees with the rightward horizontal direction; AB is parallel to DC; DA equals DC by the compass construction. Coordinates establish these relationships without supplying a numerical length.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied construction guide; diagonals and measured results are omitted.

answer.short: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with $AD=DC$, so all four sides are equal.
answer.worked: The equal corresponding $70^\circ$ angles give $AD\parallel BC$ and $AB\parallel DC$, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. The compass arc has centre $D$ and passes through $A$ and $C$, so $DA=DC$. Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, giving $AB=DC$ and $BC=AD$. Hence $AB=BC=CD=DA$, so $ABCD$ is a rhombus.

answer.short: The diagonals bisect the vertex angles and meet at $90^\circ$. For the $70^\circ$ construction, the half-angles are $35^\circ$ at $B,D$ and $55^\circ$ at $A,C$.
answer.worked:
Construct the parallel rays and use the compass arc centred at $D$ to locate $A$ with $DA=DC$. Draw the line through $A$ parallel to $DC$; its intersection with the ray from $C$ is $B$. Join $AC$ and $BD$, meeting at $M$.

Protractor measurements give $\angle DAC=\angle CAB=\angle BCA=\angle ACD=55^\circ$ and $\angle ABD=\angle DBC=\angle CDB=\angle BDA=35^\circ$. The angles at $M$ measure $90^\circ$. Thus each diagonal bisects the vertex angles through which it passes, and the diagonals are perpendicular.

spec.mathematics: Interior angles at D and B are 70 degrees; those at A and C are 110 degrees. Diagonals bisect these into 35-degree and 55-degree angles respectively and intersect perpendicularly.
